sections.title: 1. Technical Introduction
sections.body:
## Purpose
The Patient Portal provides patients of the hospital with secure, web‑based access to their electronic medical records (EMR) and related services.

## Scope
In‑scope: authentication, view of personal health information, appointment scheduling, secure messaging, audit logging, and data protection.
Out‑of‑scope: clinical decision support, billing processing, and third‑party insurance integrations.

## Definitions
- **EMR**: Electronic Medical Record system used by the hospital.
- **PHR**: Personal Health Record viewable by the patient.
- **HIPAA**: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, U.S. federal law governing protected health information (PHI).

sections.title: 2. Overall Description & System Architecture
sections.body:
The portal is a three‑tier web application:
1. **Presentation Layer** – responsive web UI accessed via modern browsers.
2. **Application Layer** – RESTful services handling business logic, authentication, and audit logging.
3. **Data Layer** – encrypted database storing patient‑specific data, synchronized with the hospital EMR.
All communication between tiers uses TLS 1.2+.
The system will be deployed within the hospital’s trusted data center to satisfy data residency requirements.

sections.title: 3. Functional Requirements
table: The system shall authenticate patients using multi‑factor authentication (MFA) in accordance with HIPAA §164.312(a)(1).
Security test suite and penetration testing
Patients shall be able to view their personal health records (PHR) retrieved securely from the EMR via HTTPS.
Patients shall schedule, modify, or cancel appointments through the portal.
Patients shall send and receive messages to/from their care team; messages shall be stored encrypted at rest.

sections.title: 4. Non-Functional Requirements
sections.body:
### Performance
- The system shall achieve a 95th percentile (P95) response latency of **≤ 250 ms** for all UI interactions (per domain benchmark).

### Security
- **Encryption at Rest**: All PHI stored in the database shall be encrypted using AES‑256 in accordance with HIPAA §164.312(e)(1)(ii).
- **Audit Logging**: Every access, modification, and transmission of PHI shall generate an immutable audit log entry meeting HIPAA §164.312(b) requirements.
- **Transport Security**: All network traffic shall be protected with TLS 1.2 or higher.
- **Access Controls**: Role‑based access control (RBAC) shall enforce least‑privilege principles.

### Reliability
- System availability shall be **≥ 99.5 %** per month, measured by uptime monitoring.
- Failover mechanisms shall provide automatic switchover within 30 seconds.

sections.title: 5. External Interface Requirements
sections.body:
#### APIs
- RESTful JSON APIs for authentication, patient data retrieval, appointment management, and messaging.
- API authentication via OAuth 2.0 with short‑lived access tokens.

#### User Interface
- Web UI compatible with Chrome, Firefox, Edge, and Safari (latest two major versions).
- Responsive design for desktop, tablet, and mobile devices.

#### Hardware / Platform
- Application servers hosted on the hospital’s on‑premises virtualized environment.
- Database servers with hardware‑based encryption modules (e.g., TPM/HSM).

sections.title: 6. System Constraints & Compliance Verification
sections.body:
### Constraints
- Deployment must reside within the hospital’s controlled data center to satisfy data residency.
- All third‑party libraries shall be vetted for HIPAA compliance.

### Compliance Verification
- **HIPAA**: Conduct a formal HIPAA compliance audit covering encryption at rest, audit logging, and access controls.
- **Performance Benchmark**: Execute load testing to confirm P95 latency ≤ 250 ms.
- **Security Testing**: Perform vulnerability scanning and penetration testing; results must be documented and remediated before release.
